name: Weighmaster: Gold Scales
subtitle: Deduce the false nugget
shortDescription: Weighing puzzles in a gold market: find the false nugget, rank hidden weights, name the short pouch. Par is exact.
longDescription:
Among the Akan of Ghana, gold dust was weighed with small cast brass weights shaped like seeds, animals and proverbs, and a weighmaster's honesty was a matter of public pride. Weighmaster borrows that sunlit market for a deduction game about the balance.

A balance can say only three things, left, right or level, and every lot on your cloth hides one puzzle. Solve it in the fewest weighings any plan could promise.

Three kinds of lot appear. In Assay, one nugget in the lot is false, heavier or lighter than its twins, and sometimes you are not told which. Drag nuggets onto the two pans, press Weigh and watch the beam swing; small marks show what each nugget could still be, and honest nuggets become helpers for the next weighing. In Order, rank stamped brass weights from lightest to heaviest using only one-against-one weighings, and the ledger remembers what follows. In Pouches, a spring scale reads grams: draw a different number of pieces from each pouch, take one reading, and name the short pouch, or the two short pouches.

The par is exact. Every lot has a par computed by a solver that checks every plan, and each of your weighings is graded against it. Three stars mean par with every weighing as sharp as possible.

Hint places the best weighing on the pans and explains it in numbers, and eight short lessons with drawings cover the three answers of the balance, spare nuggets and counting.
